dragapult-ex.title: Dragapult ex
dragapult-ex.summary: Spread damage with Phantom Dive, disrupt setup and plan a multi-Knock Out Prize turn.
steps: Establish several Drakloak for ongoing draw.
Use Budew’s Itchy Pollen and Crushing Hammer to slow the opponent.
After one of your Pokémon is Knocked Out, Unfair Stamp can reduce the opponent’s hand.
Spread damage with Phantom Dive to line up a decisive 4–6 Prize turn.
strengths: Active and Bench pressure at once
weaknesses: Stage 2 setup and mixed Energy can delay attacks
Healing or spread protection disrupts Prize mapping
against: Pressure the evolution setup before Dragapult attacks.
Protect or heal damaged Benched Pokémon to deny multi-KOs.
dragapult-ex.variantsIntro: All three builds share Dragapult ex’s Phantom Dive spread strategy. Choose a variant to see its distinct engine and trade-offs.

basic-box.title: Basic Box
basic-box.summary: A toolbox of Basic attackers supported by Mega Kangaskhan ex draw; choose attackers to exploit Weakness and Prize trades.
steps: Use Mega Kangaskhan ex to draw cards.
Identify the attacker that best fits the opponent’s board.
Use Crispin and Energy Switch to prepare that attacker.
Adapt Prize trades rather than committing to a single attacker.
weaknesses: Wrong attacker at the wrong time loses tempo
against: Disrupt access to Energy Switch and search Items.
Force awkward attacker choices and Energy commitments.

slowking.title: Slowking
slowking.summary: Use Seek Inspiration to access attacks from Pokémon without Rule Boxes by controlling the top card of the deck.
steps: Set up Slowking and Psychic Energy.
Use Academy at Night or Ciphermaniac’s Codebreaking to place a useful Pokémon on top.
Attack with Seek Inspiration to discard the top card and use its attack if eligible.
Trade efficiently using single-Prize attackers.
weaknesses: Relies on the top card of the deck
Item lock limits setup and search
Cannot copy attacks from cards already in the discard pile
against: Disrupt the top-deck setup or lock search Items.
Force awkward turns when the correct attack is not prepared.

alakazam.title: Alakazam
alakazam.summary: Grow your hand through evolution-based draw, then scale Powerful Hand damage with the number of cards held.
steps: Develop several Alakazam lines.
Evolve to draw cards and maintain a large hand.
Use Powerful Hand to place two damage counters per card in hand.
Keep a backup draw engine in case of disruption.
strengths: Scalable damage at modest Energy cost
Evolution draw can work through Item lock
weaknesses: Rare Candy and search Items are Item-lock vulnerable
against: Disrupt the hand before Powerful Hand.
Slow evolution setup with Item lock.

reference.aceSpec: Enriching Energy (reference); Prime Catcher in Dusknoir variant

ns-zoroark-ex.title: N’s Zoroark ex
ns-zoroark-ex.summary: Draw with Trade and use Night Joker to copy attacks from Benched N’s Pokémon.
steps: Establish N’s Zoroark ex and supporting N’s Pokémon.
Use Trade to cycle cards.
Choose the right Benched N’s Pokémon attack for Night Joker.
Use Pecharunt ex for non-Item switching when needed.
strengths: Pecharunt ex helps reposition Darkness Pokémon
weaknesses: Removing Benched N’s Pokémon cuts off attacks
against: Target the Benched N’s Pokémon that enable key attacks.
Interrupt assembly with Item lock or hand disruption.

festival-lead.title: Festival Lead
festival-lead.summary: Use Festival Grounds to let Festival Lead attackers attack twice per turn; Dipplin and Seaking are distinct variants.
steps: Set up the chosen attacker (Dipplin or Seaking) and Thwackey.
Use Thwackey to search for key pieces.
Keep Festival Grounds in play.
Attack twice when Festival Lead conditions are met.
weaknesses: Low-HP Pokémon are exposed to spread
against: Remove Festival Grounds.
Use Bench damage or spread to take multiple Knock Outs.

dragapult-blaziken.title: Dragapult / Blaziken
dragapult-blaziken.summary: Combine Dragapult ex spread damage with Blaziken ex Energy acceleration for sustained multi-KO pressure.
steps: Set up both Stage 2 evolution lines.
Use Blaziken ex to restore Energy.
Spread damage with Phantom Dive.
Plan a decisive 4–6 Prize turn, using Unfair Stamp after a Knock Out.
weaknesses: Reference list has no Switch effect
against: Slow Rare Candy setup with Item lock.
Trap Blaziken ex Active when retreat is prevented.

dhelmise-hide-n-sneak.title: Dhelmise — Hide ’n’ Sneak
dhelmise-hide-n-sneak.summary: Use Hide ’n’ Sneak pieces with Sinistcha spread and Spiritomb damage multiplication to create multi-KOs.
steps: Set up the Hide ’n’ Sneak engine.
Prepare Dhelmise’s attack by discarding four Pokémon with Hide ’n’ Sneak.
Spread damage counters with Sinistcha.
Use Spiritomb to multiply existing counters for multiple Knock Outs.
strengths: Mobility and protection through Hide ’n’ Sneak
weaknesses: Other Pokémon can still be trapped if the engine is unavailable
against: Interrupt the evolution engine.
Limit damage-counter buildup before Spiritomb can capitalize.

dragapult-dusknoir.title: Dragapult / Dusknoir
dragapult-dusknoir.summary: Pair Phantom Dive with Dusclops and Dusknoir damage counters to reach exact multi-KO thresholds.
steps: Develop Dragapult ex and the Dusknoir evolution line.
Spread damage with Phantom Dive.
Use Dusclops or Dusknoir to place precise counters.
Account for the Prize card conceded by Cursed Blast; use Unfair Stamp to disrupt.
strengths: Multi-KO thresholds beyond Phantom Dive alone
weaknesses: Psyduck can shut off the Dusknoir line
Rare Candy vulnerable to Item lock
against: Use Ability disruption such as Psyduck.
Track the Prize trade created by Cursed Blast.

mega-excadrill.title: Mega Excadrill
mega-excadrill.summary: Use Precious Trolley to fill the Bench and Metang’s Metal Maker to accelerate Energy to a flexible selection of attackers.
steps: Aim for turn-one Precious Trolley.
Develop Metang on the Bench.
Use Metal Maker to accelerate Metal Energy.
Choose Mega Excadrill ex or another powered attacker based on the matchup.
strengths: Fast wide Bench with Precious Trolley
weaknesses: Early Item lock blocks the key setup Item
against: Use Item lock early to stop Precious Trolley.
Disrupt Metang or trap it Active.

hydrapple.title: Hydrapple
hydrapple.summary: Attach Grass Energy through Teal Mask Ogerpon ex and Hydrapple ex, then scale Syrup Storm with Meganium.
steps: Use Teal Dance to attach Energy and draw.
Use Ripening Charge to attach Energy and heal.
Establish Meganium so Basic Grass Energy counts double for Syrup Storm.
Build Energy across the board for larger attacks.
weaknesses: Needs several Pokémon and much Energy in play
against: Disrupt Energy-attachment Abilities.
Apply pressure before Syrup Storm reaches high damage.

crustle.title: Crustle
crustle.summary: Use Mysterious Rock Inn to wall attacks from Pokémon ex while trading with single-Prize attackers.
steps: Evolve Dwebble into Crustle.
Use Mysterious Rock Inn to block damage from opposing Pokémon ex.
Attach Hero’s Cape and supportive Special Energy.
Attack with Superb Scissors or pivot to Mega Kangaskhan ex.
against: Attack with non-ex Pokémon or place damage counters through Abilities.
Exploit Fire Weakness or disrupt setup Items.

reference.energy: 13: 4 Spiky / 4 Mist / 4 Growing Grass / 1 Basic Grass

mega-lucario-ex.title: Mega Lucario ex
mega-lucario-ex.summary: Use Solrock and Lunatone for draw, Aura Jab for Energy acceleration and Mega Brave for major Knock Outs.
steps: Set up Solrock and Lunatone for draw.
Develop Mega Lucario ex as the primary attacker.
Use Aura Jab to accelerate Energy from the discard pile.
Use Mega Brave against high-HP targets; prepare Hariyama for Gust when needed.
strengths: Draw support from Solrock and Lunatone
weaknesses: Mega Lucario ex gives up three Prize cards
Mega Brave cannot be used on consecutive turns
against: Plan around Mega Brave’s following-turn restriction.
Pressure the supporting Pokémon and exploit the three-Prize liability.

mew-box.title: Mew Box
mew-box.summary: A flexible Basic Pokémon toolbox centered on Mew ex, backed by Mega Kangaskhan ex draw and a range of attackers chosen for the matchup.
steps: Use Mega Kangaskhan ex to build a steady hand while assembling the correct attacker for the matchup.
Establish Mew ex and the supporting Basic Pokémon; prioritize which attacker and Energy types are needed before committing resources.
Use Crispin and Wondrous Patch to assemble the Energy required by your chosen attacker.
Exploit the flexibility of the toolbox, switching between attackers and using Boss’s Orders or Prime Catcher to target important opposing Pokémon.
strengths: Flexible attacker selection and matchup-specific answers
Mega Kangaskhan ex supports consistent draw
Multiple Basic Pokémon options reduce reliance on one attacker
weaknesses: Correct attacker and Energy sequencing can be demanding
A broad toolbox can draw the wrong pieces at the wrong time
Bench space and multi-type Energy requirements constrain setup
against: Identify which attacker threatens your deck and disrupt its Energy setup.
Pressure the draw engine and force inefficient Prize trades.
Limit Bench space or remove key supporting Pokémon when possible.

reference.energy: Varies by list; common choices include Psychic, Telepathic Psychic, Water and Fighting Energy
reference.aceSpec: Prime Catcher (common reference choice; varies by list)
